content: Hej. Det ska finnas någon logik för ett backoffice. Det ska vara ett backoffice där ma nska kuna sköa ställen där man ka nbyta ut bilder, texter, styra blog-generatorn, ta emot oc hskriva nyhetsbrev.. men säkert någonting jag just nu inte tänker på. kan du hitta berörd kod och sedan få detta att funka fullt ut?

Goal: Identify and implement the missing/unfinished “backoffice” (admin) functionality so the site has a working admin area where we can manage content (images/text), control the blog generator, and handle newsletters end-to-end.

Context:
There should be some existing (possibly partial) logic for a backoffice/admin panel in this project, but it’s not currently working or not fully implemented. We need to locate what exists, decide the intended architecture, and complete it into a functional admin experience.

Likely involved files (search/inspect these first):
- @components/ (possible admin UI components, forms, content editors)
- @components/NewsletterSignup.js (newsletter capture UI)
- @components/ContactForm.js (email/form handling patterns)
- @blog_generator/ (blog generator scripts and GUI/control panel)
  - @blog_generator/control_panel.py
  - @blog_generator/scheduler.py
  - @blog_generator/dg97_blog_gen.py
  - @blog_generator/gui_generator.py
- @config/ (possible agent/config hooks)
  - @config/did-agents.js
- @content/posts/*.md (current blog/content storage)
- Next.js routes/pages (not shown in tree, but likely under @pages/ or @app/ depending on setup)
- API routes (likely under @pages/api/* if present)

What to do:
1) Locate existing “backoffice/admin” code and entry points
   - Search the repo for keywords: “admin”, “backoffice”, “dashboard”, “control panel”, “CMS”, “newsletter”, “blog_generator”, “scheduler”, “auth”, “login”.
   - Identify any existing routes/pages/components intended for admin use and document what’s missing/broken.

2) Define the minimal viable backoffice feature set (implement fully)
   - Admin authentication + authorization (protect all admin routes).
   - Content management:
     - Edit site texts (where they are stored today; if hardcoded, propose a migration to a JSON/MD store).
     - Replace/manage images (upload + storage strategy).
   - Blog management:
     - View existing posts from @content/posts
     - Create/edit/delete posts (or at least create/edit) via UI.
     - Trigger the Python blog generator from the backoffice (and show status/log output).
     - If scheduling exists (@blog_generator/scheduler.py), expose basic controls (enable/disable, run now).
   - Newsletter management:
     - Collect subscribers (store them somewhere persistent).
     - Compose and send newsletters (or at minimum: export list + draft sending pipeline).
     - Provide basic admin UI for viewing subscribers and sending history.

3) Decide and implement the backend integration approach
   - Determine how the Next.js app can safely call the Python blog generator:
     - Option A: server-side API route that spawns the Python script (with strict security + environment constraints).
     - Option B: separate service endpoint (if already exists) and call it from Next.js.
   - Implement robust error handling, logging, and a simple “job status” model so the UI can show progress/results.

4) Implement the admin UI
   - Add an Admin layout + navigation (e.g., “Content”, “Images”, “Blog”, “Newsletter”, “Settings”).
   - Build forms/pages for each feature above.
   - Ensure all admin pages are protected (redirect to login if not authenticated).

5) Persistence & configuration
   - Choose where to store:
     - Editable texts (e.g., a JSON file in repo, or a small DB, or a headless CMS-like local store).
     - Uploaded images (local filesystem under /public, or external storage; implement whichever is simplest for this project).
     - Newsletter subscribers + send history (file-based DB like SQLite/JSON, or whatever fits current stack).
   - Add environment variables and document them.

6) Quality expectations
   - Keep changes consistent with existing code style/components.
   - Add basic validation and security (CSRF considerations for admin actions, input validation, rate limiting for newsletter endpoints).
   - Add minimal documentation: how to access backoffice, how to run blog generator from it, where data is stored.

Deliverables:
- A working /admin (or /backoffice) area with login protection.
- Fully functional content/image editing (at least for a defined set of site content).
- Working blog generator controls integrated into the UI (trigger + status/logs).
- Newsletter subscriber management + a working send flow (or clearly implemented pipeline with a real provider if already configured).
- A short README section describing setup and usage.

Before coding:
- Inspect the repo to confirm whether this is a Next.js Pages Router or App Router project and where routes live.
- If no auth exists, propose a simple approach (e.g., NextAuth, custom password-based admin, etc.) and implement it.
